title: Cross characterization of combinatorial rectangles
statement: A subset $R \subseteq X \times Y$ is a rectangle — that is, $R = A \times B$ for some $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$ — if and only if it is closed under crossing: for all $x, x' \in X$ and $y, y' \in Y$, whenever $(x, y) \in R$ and $(x', y') \in R$, both mixed pairs $(x', y)$ and $(x, y')$ also lie in $R$.
hypotheses_covered: R is a subset of X × Y
no side hypotheses; the equivalence holds for every such R
replaced:
A set $R \subseteq X \times Y$ is a rectangle if and only if it satisfies the
\emph{cross property}: whenever $(x, y) \in R$ and $(x', y') \in R$, the mixed
pairs $(x', y)$ and $(x, y')$ also belong to $R$.
